knowledge:
- key_parameters: Y=A p x n matrix of raw methylation values (beta values), where p is the number of probes in a window and n is the number of samples ;; steps=The number of steps/iterations to run the group fused lars algorithm (e.g., steps = 30)
- alternatives: single probe analysis=MBAmethyl can be applied as an alternative to single probe analysis when multiple biological replicates are available
- when_to_use: Appropriate for smoothing densely methylated data from platforms such as Illumina 450k arrays, CHARM arrays, and bisulfite sequencing when multiple biological replicates are available
- pitfalls: The method is designed for local windows of probes rather than whole-genome analysis; the documentation recommends using a window of approximately 200 probes on real data

workflows.name: dna_methylation_smoothing
workflows.intent: Smooth raw DNA methylation beta values across neighboring probes and biological replicates using a group fused lasso model.
input: methylation_matrix.csv (A p x n matrix of raw methylation beta values where rows represent neighboring probes in a genomic window and columns represent biological samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the MBAmethyl package ;; 2. Run the smoothing algorithm on the raw methylation matrix ;; 3. Inspect and extract the smoothed methylation values using the BIC model selection criterion
workflows.code:
library(MBAmethyl)
fit <- MBAmethyl(Y, steps = 30)
str(fit$ans.bic)
theta <- fit$ans.bic
